Chapter 10: Creating a Positive Environment and Influencing Others
Let’s dive into the final step for keeping positive thinking alive—shaping your environment so it naturally supports the attitudes and behaviors you want.
Think of it like gardening. You don’t just plant a seed and walk away. You prepare the soil, pull out the weeds, and make sure everything around your plant helps it grow. In the same way, you can create surroundings that nurture optimism and personal growth.
Now, a positive environment isn’t just about what you see or touch—it’s both physical and social. On the physical side, maybe you organize your space to cut down on clutter, put up images or quotes that inspire you, or set up routines that make your day feel calmer and more in control.
On the social side, it’s about choosing to spend time with people who lift you up, encourage you, and focus on finding solutions instead of problems.
So, how can you build this kind of environment? Here are a few ideas.
First, declutter. Clear out things you don’t need, and organize your space in a way that makes you feel focused and relaxed. It’s amazing how much clearer your mind feels when your surroundings are tidy.
Next, pay attention to the kind of media you’re letting in. Try limiting negative news or entertainment. Instead, look for books, music, or podcasts that lift your spirits and give you energy.
And don’t forget about your social network. Build relationships with people who share your values and encourage you to grow. Even just one supportive friend can make a big difference.
Picture this: someone who wants to feel more optimistic might join a personal development group, or just make a habit of sharing something they’re grateful for each day with a friend. Little changes like these really add up, slowly shifting the whole mood of your daily life.
And here’s something important—when you start living with a positive outlook, you naturally influence the people around you. You don’t have to give speeches or try to convince anyone. Just by being optimistic, resilient, and kind, you inspire others to do the same.
When setbacks happen, a positive environment gives you the support to bounce back and keep going. Over time, these small habits send out ripples, spreading hope and possibility through your family, your workplace, and your community.
So, the key takeaway? Shape your environment—physically and socially—to encourage positive thinking. And remember, your energy can spark real change in others, just by being authentic and hopeful every day.
